name: Brazil

income_tax.summary: Brazilian residents pay progressive federal income tax (monthly table from January 2026: 0% to 27.5%, annualised below). From 2026 Law 15.270/2025 adds a monthly reduction that zeroes tax up to BRL 5,000 a month, phasing out at BRL 7,350, and a minimum tax on very high incomes. Employees pay progressive INSS of 7.5%-14% up to BRL 8,475.55 a month; contribuintes individuais pay 20% up to the same ceiling (11% under the simplified plan).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Contribuinte individual: 20% of income between the minimum wage (BRL 1,621.00) and the ceiling BRL 8,475.55 a month (maximum BRL 1,695.11); the simplified plan is 11% of the minimum wage only (BRL 178.31) with reduced benefits; PwC also mentions 5%, 11% or 20% depending on conditions. Self-employed income of residents is taxed through the monthly carne-leao on the same progressive table. Employee effective rate 0.1166 = maximum monthly INSS BRL 988.09 / ceiling BRL 8,475.55, computed from the progressive table. Contribuinte individual rates (5% low-income optional/MEI, 11% simplified, 20% normal) confirmed on the INSS 2026 table page.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No municipal income tax on individuals (Sao Paulo levies ISS services tax on businesses, not modelled). Brackets are the January 2026 monthly table multiplied by 12.

open_questions: Brackets are on taxable income after INSS and the simplified deduction. Law 15.270/2025 (art. 3-A reduction, read on the Receita 2026 tables page) zeroes annual tax up to BRL 60,000 of taxable income and phases out linearly (BRL 8,429.73 - 0.095575 x income) to zero at BRL 88,200; it is not in the brackets because it affects only incomes below BRL 88,200, well under both personas (nomad USD 60k, expat USD 150k).

Minimum tax (art. 16-A of Law 15.270, read in the Planalto text 2026-10-15): from tax year 2026, individuals with total receipts above BRL 600,000 owe at least a rate on all receipts (including exempt and exclusively-taxed income) that rises linearly from 0% at BRL 600,000 to 10% at BRL 1,200,000 (rate = receipts/60,000 - 10), less ordinary IRPF, withholding and the art. 16-B reducer. It is a floor of at most 10% of receipts, below the ordinary 27.5% marginal scale on salary or professional income, so it does not change the brackets for the expat (USD 150k) or the nomad; it bites only when much of the income is exempt or taxed separately (dividends, financial income).
13th salary and dividend withholding (10% above BRL 50,000/month) not modelled.

Employee rate 0.1166 is an effective rate at the ceiling: maximum INSS BRL 988.09 (7.5/9/12/14% progressive table, Portaria MPS/MF 13 of 9 Jan 2026, read on gov.br/inss) / ceiling BRL 8,475.55; below the ceiling the effective rate is lower.

PwC (deductions page, 2026): taxpayers may instead take a standard deduction of 20% of gross taxable income capped at BRL 17,640 from January 2026, 'in lieu of the above itemised deductions' (including INSS). Above about BRL 88,200 a year it exceeds the maximum INSS (about BRL 11,860), so social_security_deductible = 1 and a bracket base 'after INSS and the simplified deduction' must not apply both; check how the model combines them.

regimes.name: Digital nomad visa (VITEM XIV)
regimes.description: Temporary residence for remote workers with no Brazilian employment relationship. Requires proof of at least USD 1,500 a month from a foreign source or USD 18,000 in bank funds, health insurance and a clean record. It does not change tax: holders without a Brazilian employment contract become tax resident after 183 days of presence within 12 months and are then taxed on worldwide income at ordinary rates.
regimes.duration_note: One year, renewable once for another year at the Federal Police (per the embassy page).

residence_routes: EU and US citizens can enter visa-free as tourists but cannot work; remote workers use the VITEM XIV digital nomad visa (USD 1,500 monthly foreign income or USD 18,000 funds), valid one year, renewable once. Skilled employees need a work visa tied to a Brazilian employer (temporary residence with work authorisation from the Ministry of Labour); permanent residence routes (family, investment, long residence) exist but were not researched. Nationals of Mercosur and associated states have a separate residence-agreement route.
open_questions: Minimum tax (art. 16-A, Law 15.270) read in the statute: a floor of at most 10% of receipts, not reflected in the brackets (see income tax open questions).
2-bedroom rent is a listing-platform average with an unclear bedroom filter.
